agents.reasoning: Primary documents first: the four 2026 letters, the Q3 10-Q and the Q3 call. Q3 FY2026: revenue 12.87B (+12%), margin 34.6%, FY2026 guide 51.1B / 31.5%, ad revenue cut to ~2.7B, ~1,000 job cuts, record $4.8B buyback; H1 view hours +2% (Q2 letter). The stock fell 46% in a year (WBD bid and walk-away, then growth/engagement worries and the ad cut); it trades at 16.3x Street NTM EPS. Build: revenue = members x ARM by quarter (members 301.6M end-2024 -> 325M end-2025; 2026-28 growth slowing to ~4.5%), ARM +4.5% from price rounds and ads less mix; cost of revenues +8.5%/+8% (content amortization +9.5% YTD), opex nearly flat in 2027 after the cuts. Result: margin 31.6%/33.7%/34.4%, GAAP EPS FY2027 3.90 (Zacks 3.74, +4%), FY2028 4.53 (4.43, +2%). Guidance record: margin guides beaten 3 of 3 years (median +8.5%), quarterly revenue guides within 1%; we sit inside the FY guides because the 9M actuals fix them. Multiple: 5 peers, median 18.56x, shrunk k=0.8 to 16.75x. Downside (P10) cuts member and ARM growth by 2.5 and 2 pts and the multiple by 4 turns; upside (P90) adds 1.5/1.5 pts, lower opex and 3.5 turns. Moderately conservative per project rules; research done mostly by WebFetch of filings.

agents.method_text: NTM P/E 16.59x (peer median 17.66x shrunk toward NFLX's 16.33x with k = 0.8) on our own NTM GAAP EPS of ~$4.09 at 2027-11-17 (mostly FY2028 EPS $4.27, 3.7% below the $4.43 consensus), from a quarterly UCAN/International revenue build (FY2027 +8.3%, FY2028 +7.6%) and content-amortization/cost build (EBIT margin 32.6% / 33.3%).

inputs_detail.derivation: UCAN = paid members x ARM. Members: Antenna data (Reuters, source 9) show monthly US subscriber losses through September 2026 and no net adds in 2026; Netflix disputes it, so we take members at about -0.5% y/y through 2027 and ~0% in 2028 (not the steeper decline Antenna implies). ARM: the 2026 US price change landed in Q2'26 ('partial-quarter impact', Q2'26 letter, source 4) and Q3'26 UCAN grew +11.0% with flat members, so ARM ~+11% until the change laps: Q4'26 +11.0%, Q1'27 +9.5%, Q2'27 +7.5% (partial lap). After the lap ARM growth = ads + plan mix only: Netflix ads ~$2.7B in 2026 (source 14) growing to ~$4.2B in 2027 adds ~2.5-3 pts in UCAN where ads are concentrated, so H2'27 +4.5%. Netflix's US price steps came in Jan 2025 and spring 2026 (sources 6, 4), ~15 months apart, so we place the next one in early 2028: Q1'28 +5.5%, Q2-Q3'28 +7.0%, Q4'28 +6.5% (ads maturing). Other evidence-based builds: (a) Antenna's no-net-adds reading taken at face value as members -2% a year: UCAN FY2027 growth ~4.5% instead of ~6.4%; (b) a second US price change in H2 2027 (Netflix's 15-month cadence from spring 2026): FY2027 UCAN ~+8%; (c) Spotify's Q3'26 ARPU +7.5% cc on price increases with 6M net adds (source 21) shows subscription price power still works in a mature market. The upside and downside cases move this driver by +2.5 / -3.5 pts.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Antenna's member losses taken literally (-2%/yr) cut FY2027 UCAN to ~+4.5% and the research target (12m) by ~4%; a 2027 US price step lifts it ~+5%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3'26 International grew +12.6% reported, ~+10.9% F/X neutral (EMEA 9%, LATAM 12%, APAC 15% F/X neutral, weighted by Q3 revenue; source 1). We hold F/X flat from here, so reported ~ F/X neutral after Q4'26. Members: APAC/India view hours +24% and India revenue +18% (source 1), and the ad tier launches in 15 more countries from March 2027 (9 EMEA + Colombia, Peru, New Zealand first; source 14), so members grow ~5-6% in 2027. ARM +3-4% from the H1'26 price changes in Mexico and Spain lapping and ads. Path: Q4'26 +12.0% (some F/X tailwind left), 2027 +10.5% / +10.0% / +9.5% / +9.0% (decelerating as the 2026 price changes lap), 2028 +8.5% and +8.0% in Q4 (ad-tier countries in the base). Other evidence-based builds: (a) hold the Q3'26 F/X-neutral +10.9% through 2027: FY2027 International ~+11% instead of ~+9.7%; (b) EMEA's slower F/X-neutral 9% across all regions as markets mature (Greenlight/Hub on churn, source 24): ~+8.5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Holding the Q3'26 F/X-neutral ~10.9% through 2027 adds ~+2% to the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4'26 5,250 = +10.2% y/y: Netflix guided FY2026 content amortization ~+10% (Q2'26 letter, source 4), which needs Q4 ~5,300; Q3'26 grew only +5.8% and 'higher growth in H1 than H2', so slightly below the guide-implied Q4 (FY2026 17,965, +9.4%). 2027 +6.5% and 2028 +6.0% per quarter: content cash spend runs ~1.1x amortization (source 1), the new content chief and ~6% headcount cut point to discipline, while live sports (three NFL games in Q4'26, source 9/Reuters) and the Paramount+HBO Max combination (~200M subs, source 18) bid up rights. Other builds: (a) ~+10% a year as in 2026 (rights inflation): FY2027 EBIT -$0.65B; (b) +5.8% (Q3'26 run-rate): +$0.12B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Content amortization growing ~10% a year (rights inflation after the Paramount-WBD merger) cuts FY2028 EBIT ~$1.3B, ~-7% to the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 actual ratios 33.3% / 32.3% / 32.5% ran ~1 pt above 2025's 32.0% / 31.3% / 31.6% ex Brazil (ad-tech, live and games build-out). agents.reasoning: Industry lane. The chain says Netflix's demand is flat in the US and still growing abroad: Antenna (via Reuters) shows no US net adds through September 2026, Apptopia shows non-openers up 16.6% y/y, H1 view hours rose only 2%, and YouTube holds 2x Netflix's TV time in Nielsen's Gauge. Pricing still works (Q3 UCAN +11% on the spring price change; Spotify's +7.5% cc ARPU shows the subscription model holds), but the US price step laps in Q2 2027. Competitors: Disney's streaming profit doubled (11.5% margin) and Paramount will merge HBO Max with Paramount+ (~200M subs), both raising content-rights pressure; YouTube's own ad growth slowed to 9%, so the CTV ad pool is not booming for anyone, and Netflix cut its 2026 ad outlook 10% to $2.7B. Build: two-region quarterly revenue (UCAN growth 11% -> ~4.5% in H2 2027 -> ~7% in 2028 with a next price step; International ~10% -> 8.5%), content amortization +6.5%/+6%, non-content costs down ~0.3 pt on the headcount cut. FY2027 revenue $55.4B (+8.3%) is below the 'sustained double-digit' aim; FY2027 EPS $3.73 matches the $3.74 consensus because our margin is higher, and FY2028 EPS $4.27 is 3.7% below the $4.43 consensus. Value: P/E 16.59x (whole-company peers DIS/SONY/SPOT median 17.66x shrunk to NFLX's 16.33x, k = 0.8) on NTM EPS ~$4.09 gives the research target (12m). Downside (P10) and upside (P90) move the regional growth drivers, costs and the multiple; the left tail is wider, matching the -46% year. Outside ad forecasts (WARC Feb 2026, Motley Fool Sept 2026) were overtaken by the Oct 20 cut and are reconciled, not used as the path. Research was limited by blocked consensus pages (no revenue consensus) and paywalled trade press (Puck, MediaPost).

inputs_detail.derivation: Built from price, members and ads, not from a past trend. Price: the US list-price rise posted 2026-03-26 (ads $7.99 -> $8.99, +12.5%; Standard +$2 to $19.99, +11%; Premium +$2 to $26.99, +8%; src 18) lifts UCAN ARM from Q2'26 and laps in Q2'27. That is why Q3'26 grew 11.0%, and growth steps down to about 6% in Q2'27 when only members and ads remain. Members: Antenna shows monthly US subscriber losses through September (src 22), and Bloomberg/Wells Fargo show viewing per member falling (src 14, 13), so I assume US household growth is flat to +1% and ARM mix shifts toward the ads plan. Ads: the 2026 ad forecast was cut to $2.7B from $3.0B on slower ad-product rollout (src 1); UCAN is most of it, adding about 2 points of UCAN growth in FY27. I give a further US price rise in H2'27 about 50% weight (cadence: Jan 2025 and Mar 2026), which supports FY27 Q3-Q4 at +6.5-7%. Q4'26 at +11.0% (Q3'26 +11.0%; price still in the base; NFL Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas games, src 15). Path: Q4 FY26 +11.0%; FY27 Q1-Q4 +9.0%, +6.0%, +6.5%, +7.0%; FY28 Q1-Q4 +6.2%, +6.4%, +6.1%, +5.9% y/y. Alternatives sized: (a) Street FY27 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%, src 9) applied pro rata is about +2.2% on UCAN; (b) the Q3'26 rate held (+11%) is a carried trend and is rejected.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Street FY27 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%) vs ours; if price increases keep landing every ~14 months with no churn, the regions run 1-2 points faster and the research target (12m) rises about 6%

inputs_detail.derivation: Content amortization is the margin lever. FY26 amortization growth was guided at about 10% vs revenue +13% (src 4). That leverage gave 2026 Q1-Q3 ratios of 48.1%, 48.1%, 47.2% vs 49.9%, 48.1%, 53.6% in 2025 (Q3'25 includes Brazil's ~$0.6B non-income tax charge; about 48.2% without it). Skeptic case for FY27: the new content leadership and Wolfe's 'higher spending fails to lift engagement' (src 12) point to amortization growing about as fast as the slower revenue, so I allow only about 0.3 points of leverage (FY27 48.8% vs FY26 49.1%) and about 0.5 points in FY28. Q4 is seasonally high (54.1% Q4'25, live sports). Alternative: amortization +10% on the Street's +10.7% revenue gives about 48.4% (-0.4 point, roughly +1.5% on EPS).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Street-style 1 point a year of margin expansion lifts FY28 EPS about 3%

FY27 takes part of the layoff savings (about 6% of headcount; src 16). Against that sit ad-tech and ad-sales build-out in 15 new countries and marketing to rebuild engagement. Net, FY27 is 18.8% vs FY26 19.4%, and FY28 18.6%.

Buybacks: Q3'26 63.9M shares for $4,797M (about $75); $22.3B authorization left. At my shareholder returns of $12.2-13.5B a year and a $62-70 price, that retires 180-215M shares (4.3-5.1%). Option dilution is about 0.3-0.5% a year (diluted shares fell 3.3% y/y, 4,340.4 -> 4,195.1, on $12.9B TTM buybacks at higher prices). Net -4.2%.

agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. The downside evidence is broad and current. Revenue growth has slowed four quarters running (Q1'26 16.2%, Q2 13.4%, Q3 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%). The FY26 range ended below its first midpoint. Ad revenue was cut 10% ($3.0B -> $2.7B). Bloomberg and Wells Fargo show viewing per member falling (Wells: about -8% per household in H1), and Antenna shows US subscriber losses through September. YouTube has twice Netflix's US TV time (Nielsen, August). HSBC, Wells Fargo, Needham and Wolfe downgraded, a Seeking Alpha Sell followed, and hedge-fund holders fell (146 -> 121). Insider sales (Hastings, Neumann, March 2026) are routine option exercises and carry little signal. Credit is not a risk: net debt is 6.9B on about 16B of EBITDA, the July 2026 10-year priced at 5.25%, and the revolver covenant is 3x EBITDA/interest, well clear. Weighed honestly, the business is still growing about 11% with a 31.5% margin and buying back about 5% of its shares a year, so the risk is a de-rating and estimate cuts, not distress. Model: four regional drivers built from price (the March-2026 US rise laps in Q2'27), members (flat to +1% in the US) and the 2027 ad-tier launches, with no currency gain carried forward. FY27 revenue comes to 55.4B (+8.5%), 2.1% below the Street's 56.6B. Content-amortization leverage is limited (cost ratio -0.3 points), so the EBIT margin is 32.4% in FY27 and 33.1% in FY28. EPS is about $3.59 and $4.14, 4% and 7% below Zacks (3.74 and 4.43). Value: NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon x 16.75x (peer median 18.56x shrunk to NFLX's 16.33x with k = 0.8). Downside and upside move the drivers (revenue levels -6%/+3.5%, cost ratios +2.5/-1.5 points) and the multiple (-4.0/+4.5 turns); the downside sits further from base, a fatter left tail. Research was limited: Twelve Data's estimate, insider and price-target endpoints require a paid plan; SEC folder indexes refused plain requests, so filings were read through WebFetch; Puck, NST and MarketBeat pages could not be read.

Alternative-data read: Apptopia shows US non-openers +16.6% y/y in Q3 2026 (src 13), Nielsen has Netflix at 7.7% of US TV vs YouTube 15.8% (src 14, 15), H1 2026 view hours only +2% (src 5): all point to saturating volume, hence the deceleration.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the Apptopia and Nielsen engagement slide (src 13, 14) turns into churn, 2027 adds could halve to ~6M: revenue -1.5% by FY2028 and the research target (12m) -6.2% (engine: 65.00 vs 69.32).

agents.reasoning: Start: the stock is at $59.68, down 46% in a year, at 16.3x NTM consensus EPS. The fall followed three things: revenue growth slowing each quarter (16% -> 13% -> 12% -> ~11.5% guided for Q4), the cut to the 2026 ad target ($3.0B -> $2.7B), and evidence of weaker engagement. Lane work (alternative data) tested whether the engagement worry is real. It is, but it shows up mostly in volume, not yet in churn. Apptopia (via Bloomberg/A.V. Club) has US subscribers not opening the app up 16.6% y/y in Q3. Nielsen's Gauge (TheWrap, Tubefilter) puts Netflix at 7.7% of US TV against YouTube's record 15.8%. The Entertainment Strategy Guy and Hub Intel Substack show returning shows losing audiences and per-user viewing falling. Stocktwits retail sentiment is extremely bearish. On the other side, Antenna data still shows strong Premium uptake among cord-cutters, and the company says price rises in the US, Mexico and Spain went as expected. My read: pricing still works but member growth is saturating, so the base case decelerates memberships (+4.6% in 2026, +3.5%, +2.8%) and keeps ARM at +3-3.5%, below the 2026 pace. Ads come from company statements (250M+ monthly active ad viewers, 15 new markets in 2027), not the stale Omdia path, which I reconciled. Guidance record: quarterly revenue beats have shrunk to about zero in 2026 and margin beats came from expense timing, so Q4 sits just under the guide. Content cost (+7.5%/+6.5%) and opex give 33.0%/34.1% margins. EPS ends 2-3% under consensus. Valuation follows the playbook: P/E on our own GAAP EPS with the k = 0.8 shrink toward a thin 3-name whole-company peer median (17.66x), giving 16.59x and $69.32 (+16%). That is mostly buyback-driven EPS growth at a flat multiple. Downside (P10, $42.24) has the engagement slide turning into churn, an ad slip, a content push and a de-rating to ~13.6x. Upside (P90, $102.86) has ads and pricing working and a partial return of the premium. Engine-sized judgment calls over 5% are listed in gap_note for Kilian. Research used about 25 searches and fetches; X/Twitter, Reddit and several data-vendor pages (Apptopia, MediaPost/Antenna, Puck, eMarketer, MarketBeat) blocked fetching, so I relied on reachable relays of them and flagged each relay. No option prices were consulted.

agents.reasoning: Lane: base rates, history, events. (1) What happened: revenue growth slowed four quarters running (16.2% to 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%), the 2026 ad goal was cut to ~$2.7B, H1 view hours grew 2% and Netflix's US TV share fell from 8.8% to 7.7% while YouTube hit 15.8% [1][6][18][19]; the stock fell 46% in a year to a 52-week low. Earnings still grow ~20% and FCF (~$12B) all goes to buybacks. (2) Guidance record: first annual revenue guides were beaten by +1.5% (FY2024) and +3.9% (FY2025), margins by 2.7 and 1.5pts, but FY2026 lands inside its first range and on its 31.5% margin guide, and quarterly beats have shrunk to ~0.1-0.8%: the beat habit has ended, so we do not add one [4][7][8][9]. (3) Build: regional y/y growth (members, price, ads) fading by ~1pt a year per the growth-persistence evidence [23] to +9.4% in 2027 and +8.4% in 2028 (1-2.5% under consensus [13]); cost of revenues +7.5%/+7%, opex +6% on a base cleared of deal and layoff costs, giving 33.5% / 34.5% margins (consensus 33.3% / 35.1%). (4) Value: P/E 16.82x on our NTM EPS ~$4.27 (3.97B shares at the horizon; consensus NTM ~$4.35) = $71.90. NFLX's own 2022 trough was ~15.6x trailing [10][15], so the exit multiple already sits at the low end of its history. (5) Distribution: after -40%+ years the six analogs returned a median +63% but the two maturity de-ratings (PYPL -27%, DIS +4%) are the closer fit [15][16]; Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20% [17]. Downside (P10) $43.24 cuts growth 3pts and the multiple to ~11.8x; upside (P90) $104.37 adds 2pts of growth and re-rates to ~21.8x. The left tail is fatter. Not driver-linked: none (one P/E leg). Research limits: Zacks, MarketBeat, chartmill and Northeast Times pages were blocked; consensus revenue came from MarketScreener, EPS from Nasdaq/Zacks.
